steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper analyzing the diffusion process in SE(3)-invariant space for 3D structure generation. Explain why existing approaches fall short, what our differential-geometry analysis and projection-free sampling contribute, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:

- Difficulty of diffusion on the distance-matrix manifold
- Approaches that avoid the manifold

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Background
  - growing interest: diffusion-based generative models to sample 3D structures (cite)
  - promising at capturing wide distribution of 3D coordinates; roto-translational property of SE(3)-invariant space a key factor (cite)
- Distance-matrix manifold
  - inter-node distance matrix inherently SE(3)-invariant; natural, flexible choice for diffusion
  - need to estimate score function on manifold (cite)
  - geometry highly irregular, non-trivial; accurate estimation hard
  - simplifications: Gaussian (cite), Maxwell-Boltzmann (cite) assumptions -> sub-optimal
  - no systematic in-depth analysis so far
- Avoiding the manifold
  - SE(3) group methods (cite): prior knowledge to overcome SE(3)-invariance
  - molecular conformation: RDkit for local 3D structures, diffusion for torsional angles (cite)
  - protein generation: SE(3) Lie group, properties depend on bond angles and lengths (cite)
  - task-specific, inflexible for generic 3D coordinate generation
  - point clouds: no explicit SE(3)-invariance design (cite); diffusion on node embeddings; transformers learn invariance implicitly, brute force
- Sampling problems
  - no mathematical understanding -> reverse ODE/SDE in SE(3)-invariant space opaque
  - naive Langevin dynamics (LD), thousands of steps (cite)
  - modern solvers (DPM solver, high-order solvers) (cite) -> unmeaningful structures; Fig. 1 example
  - Riemannian manifold framework (cite): projection each step, can't be accelerated
- Our work
  - differential geometry + projected differential equations
  - derive transformation: inter-point distance change <-> coordinate shift; linear operations, bounded errors, mimic projection
  - projection-free SDE and ODE formulations for reverse process
  - experiments: molecular conformation generation (cite), pose skeleton generation (cite); high quality with few steps
  - contributions: accurate modeling via adjacency matrices; mappings Cartesian space <-> matrix manifold, linear approx. of projection; projection-free sampling, simple acceleration

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Recently there has been more and more interest in using diffusion-based generative models to sample 3-dimensional (3D) structures. These approaches have shown promising modeling ability for capturing the wide distribution of 3D coordinates, and incorporating the inherent roto-translational property of SE(3)-invariant space is considered one of the key factors that may lead to these successes.

For 3D structures, the inter-node distance matrix is inherently SE(3)-invariant, so it is a natural and flexible choice for modeling the underlying diffusion process. To do diffusion-based generation on this manifold, it is essential to estimate the associated score function. Unfortunately the geometry of this manifold is very irregular and non-trivial, which makes mathematical and accurate estimation very difficult. Some recent works simplify the diffusion process with Gaussian or Maxwell-Boltzmann assumptions, but these heuristics can result in sub-optimal performance. So far, the existing literature has not systematically done an in-depth analysis of the diffusion process in this manifold.

At the same time, some other attempts try to avoid working directly on this manifold. Some methods address the SE(3) group, which gives a way to get around the SE(3)-invariance obstacle using prior knowledge. For molecular conformation generation tasks, some works use RDkit to first generate local 3D structures, and then use diffusion techniques to get torsional angles. Alternatively, models for protein generation go into the SE(3) Lie group, and they make use of the fact that protein properties intrinsically depend on bond angles and lengths. But these modeling schemes only apply to specific tasks and are not flexible to extend to generic 3D coordinate generation. For point clouds, most existing studies do not explicitly design for SE(3)-invariance. Instead they usually apply diffusion techniques directly on node embeddings. Some of them get good performance by using transformer architectures, and expect the model to learn SE(3)-invariance implicitly in brute force.

- Sampling problems
  - no mathematical understanding -> reverse ODE/SDE in SE(3)-invariant space opaque
  - naive Langevin dynamics (LD), thousands of steps (cite)
  - modern solvers (DPM solver, high-order solvers) (cite) -> unmeaningful structures; Fig. 1 example
  - Riemannian manifold framework (cite): projection each step, can't be accelerated
- Our work
  - differential geometry + projected differential equations
  - derive transformation: inter-point distance change <-> coordinate shift; linear operations, bounded errors, mimic projection
  - projection-free SDE and ODE formulations for reverse process
  - experiments: molecular conformation generation (cite), pose skeleton generation (cite); high quality with few steps
  - contributions: accurate modeling via adjacency matrices; mappings Cartesian space <-> matrix manifold, linear approx. of projection; projection-free sampling, simple acceleration

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Recently there has been more and more interest in using diffusion-based generative models to sample 3-dimensional (3D) structures. These approaches have shown promising modeling ability for capturing the wide distribution of 3D coordinates, and incorporating the inherent roto-translational property of SE(3)-invariant space is considered one of the key factors that may lead to these successes.

For 3D structures, the inter-node distance matrix is inherently SE(3)-invariant, so it is a natural and flexible choice for modeling the underlying diffusion process. To do diffusion-based generation on this manifold, it is essential to estimate the associated score function. Unfortunately the geometry of this manifold is very irregular and non-trivial, which makes mathematical and accurate estimation very difficult. Some recent works simplify the diffusion process with Gaussian or Maxwell-Boltzmann assumptions, but these heuristics can result in sub-optimal performance. So far, the existing literature has not systematically done an in-depth analysis of the diffusion process in this manifold.

At the same time, some other attempts try to avoid working directly on this manifold. Some methods address the SE(3) group, which gives a way to get around the SE(3)-invariance obstacle using prior knowledge. For molecular conformation generation tasks, some works use RDkit to first generate local 3D structures, and then use diffusion techniques to get torsional angles. Alternatively, models for protein generation go into the SE(3) Lie group, and they make use of the fact that protein properties intrinsically depend on bond angles and lengths. But these modeling schemes only apply to specific tasks and are not flexible to extend to generic 3D coordinate generation. For point clouds, most existing studies do not explicitly design for SE(3)-invariance. Instead they usually apply diffusion techniques directly on node embeddings. Some of them get good performance by using transformer architectures, and expect the model to learn SE(3)-invariance implicitly in brute force.

Since existing works lack a mathematical understanding, there are more concerns. Without accurate modeling, the reverse ODE and SDE formats of the diffusion process in SE(3)-invariant space are still opaque. So existing approximations usually sample 3D structures with naive Langevin dynamics (LD) with thousands of steps. Directly applying modern solvers (e.g., DPM solver and high-order solvers) is problematic and produces unmeaningful structures. Fig. 1 shows an example. Also, a coarse diffusive framework on Riemannian manifold needs a projection operation on each sampling step, so it also cannot be accelerated effectively.

To better understand the diffusion process in SE(3)-invariant space and help downstream tasks, in this paper we systematically investigate the correlated diffusion process in this space from the point of view of differential geometry and projected differential equations. For this, we mathematically derive the transformation between inter-point distance change and coordinate shift, which gives linear operations with bounded errors that mimic a projection into SE(3)-invariant space. With this we propose projection-free SDE and ODE formulations to reverse the diffusion process. These findings give useful insights into the mathematical mechanism of diffusion in SE(3)-invariant space. We do extensive experiments on molecular conformation generation and pose skeleton generation. Our scheme can sample high-quality 3D coordinates with only a few steps. To summarize, our contributions are:

- • We systematically investigate how to model diffusion-based generation in SE(3)-invariant space accurately, by considering the adjacency matrices for 3D coordinate generation tasks.

- • We analyze the mappings between the SE(3)-invariant Cartesian space and the matrix manifold, and propose a linear operation that approximates the projection operation with bounded errors.

- • We propose a new projection-free sampling scheme that solves the reverse SDE and ODE via samplings between coordinates and adjacency matrices, which allows simple acceleration.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recently, there has been increasing interest in using diffusion-based generative models to sample 3-dimensional (3D) structures [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]. These approaches have demonstrated promising modeling ability in capturing the wide distribution of 3D coordinates, wherein the incorporation of the inherent roto-translational property of SE(3)-invariant space is considered as one of the key factors potentially leading to these successes [9].

For 3D structures, the inter-node distance matrix is inherently equipped with SE(3)-invariance, and is thus a natural and flexible choice for modeling the underlying diffusion process. To perform diffusion-based generation on this manifold, estimating the associated score function is essential [10]. Unfortunately, the geometry over this manifold is highly irregular and non-trivial, which makes mathematical and accurate estimation very difficult. While some recent works simplify the diffusion process with Gaussian [3] or Maxwell-Boltzmann [5] assumptions, these heuristics may result in sub-optimal performance. So far, the existing literature has not systematically undertaken an in-depth analysis of the diffusion process in this manifold.

In parallel, some other attempts seek to avoid direct manipulations on this manifold. Certain methodologies address the SE(3) group [11], offering a means to overcome the SE(3)-invariance obstacle through prior knowledge. In the context of molecular conformation generation tasks, specific endeavors employ RDkit to initially generate local 3D structures, subsequently employing diffusion techniques to derive torsional angles [4]. Alternatively, models geared towards protein generation delve into the SE(3) Lie group, capitalizing on the intrinsic dependency of protein properties on bond angles and lengths [12,13]. However, the applicability of these modeling schemes is confined to specific tasks and proves inflexible to extend to generic 3D coordinate generation. In the case of point clouds, the majority of existing studies do not explicitly formulate designs for SE(3)-invariance [14,15,16,17]. Instead, they usually apply diffusion techniques directly on node embeddings. Notably, some achieve commendable performance by leveraging transformer architectures, anticipating the model to implicitly learn SE(3)-invariance in brute force.

The lack of mathematical understanding in existing works raises more concerns. Without accurate modeling, the reverse ODE and SDE formats of the diffusion process in SE(3)-invariant space remains opaque. Therefore, existing approximations usually sample 3D structures via naive Langevin dynamics (LD) with thousands of steps [1,3]. Directly applying modern solvers (e.g., DPM solver and high-order solvers [19,18]) is problematic and produces unmeaningful structures. See Fig. 1 for an example. Also, a coarse diffusive framework on Riemannian manifold [9] requires projection operation on each sampling step, failing to be effectively accelerated as well.

To better understand the diffusion process in SE(3)-invariant space and facilitate downstream tasks, in this paper, we systematically investigate the correlated diffusion process in this space from the perspective of differential geometry and projected differential equations. To this end, we mathematically derive the transformation between inter-point distance change and coordinate shift, delivering linear operations with bounded errors to mimic a projection into SE(3)-invariant space. As such, we propose projection-free SDE and ODE formulations to reverse the diffusion process. These findings give useful insights into the mathematical mechanism of diffusion in SE(3)-invariant space. We conduct extensive experiments on molecular conformation generation [20] and pose skeleton generation [21]. Our scheme can sample high-quality 3D coordinates with only a few steps. In summary, our contributions are:

- • We systematically investigate how to accurately model the diffusion-based generation in SE(3)-invariant space by considering the adjacency matrices for 3D coordinate generation tasks.

- • We analyze the mappings between the SE(3)-invariant Cartesian space and matrix manifold and propose a linear operation to approximate the projection operation with bounded errors.

- • We propose a novel projection-free sampling scheme by solving the reverse SDE and ODE via samplings between coordinates and adjacency matrices, allowing for simple acceleration.
